design: Three labels per diagnosis: (1) deterministic keyword scan (the harness gate), (2) codex-as-judge semantic grade against expected_diagnosis, (3) human label by the scenario author (ground truth). Agreement measured label-vs-human.

agents.diagnosed: codex exec (CLI default model; diagnose mode has no --model pin — recorded as a limitation)
agents.judge: codex exec, same CLI, judge prompt built from expected_diagnosis (shares model variance with the diagnosed agent — known limitation)

sample.note: Agent claimed NO overlap prevention existed; the code had withoutOverlapping(10) with an expiry shorter than the documented 45-minute runtime. Keyword vocabulary matched, facts were wrong. First documented over-credit flavor: factual misread.

Agent identified the true root cause (provider side effect inside the transaction survives rollback, orphaning the reservation) but proposed distributed-saga/outbox/compensation machinery as the remedy — violating the scenario's safe_fix_constraints ('no new database tables; no queue-based restructuring'). Expected remedy: commit the local order first, then reserve. Second documented over-credit flavor: remedy misalignment. Judge caught it; keywords cannot grade fix direction.

summary.keyword_misses: Both misses are over-credits (keyword passed a diagnosis a human graded partial): scheduler-overlap (factual misread) and transaction-boundary (remedy misalignment). Keywords never under-credit a correct diagnosis in this sample.
summary.conclusion: At the pre-registered >=10 sample size, the judge agrees with the human author on every case, including both partials the keywords passed. Keyword scoring stays as the deterministic floor; the judge is trusted as the semantic layer.
